final.content:
# Comparative report: heat-pump dryers for a Melbourne heritage terrace

## Executive conclusion

For a household drying 6–8 loads each week, the **LG DVH9-09W is the best overall purchase**, provided its operating noise is acceptable after an in-home or retailer demonstration. It combines a 9 kg capacity, current Australian support, the strongest available CHOICE brand-reliability signal, an automatic condenser-cleaning system and a substantially lower purchase price than the Bosch.

The **Bosch WTX88M20AU** is the best documented choice for low energy consumption and noise: 98 kWh per labelled year and 62 dB(A). Its drawbacks are its smaller 8 kg capacity, discontinued status, high price, and consumer reports of inaccessible lint accumulation or condensate-system faults despite the “self-cleaning” condenser.

The exact **Samsung DV90T6240LH should not be selected for a new Australian installation** unless the seller proves that the supplied suffix is Australian-compliant, GEMS-registered, covered by Samsung Australia and eligible for local service. The available performance figures are European/UK figures, not directly comparable Australian AS/NZS label results. Australian availability of at least some parts is evident, but exact-model local product and support coverage is not.

For a heritage-listed terrace with limited ventilation, all three have the important advantage of being **ventless heat-pump condenser dryers**. They do not normally require a wall or façade penetration, avoiding the principal heritage-planning problem associated with a vented dryer.

---

## 1. Headline comparison

| Factor | Bosch WTX88M20AU | LG DVH9-09W | Samsung DV90T6240LH |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Nominal capacity | 8 kg | 9 kg | 9 kg |
| Australian market status | Australian model, but Bosch now says “no longer available” | Current Australian product/support listing | Exact model principally documented in UK/EU sources; Australian status uncertain |
| Australian energy label | 10 stars; 98 kWh/year | 9 stars; 129 kWh/year | No Australian GEMS result established |
| Label-equivalent energy per cycle | 1.885 kWh | 2.481 kWh | 1.54 kWh/cycle from older EU/UK data; newer EPREL entry says 1.05 kWh, illustrating non-comparable standards/data |
| Published noise | 62 dB(A) | No reliable manufacturer figure located | 63 dB in UK specification |
| Dimensions, H × W × D | 842 × 598 × 613 mm; about 665 mm including handle | 850 × 600 × 690 mm; 1,115 mm door open | 850 × 600 × 600 mm |
| Condenser maintenance | Automatic/self-cleaning; lint filter still requires cleaning | Automatic condenser cleaning; dual lint filter after every use | User-cleanable heat exchanger, generally monthly/when alerted; lint filter every load |
| Standard warranty | 2 years | 2 years parts and labour; additional 8 years parts-only on inverter compressor and motor | Samsung Australia generally gives dryers 24 months, but imported exact model may not qualify |
| CHOICE reliability evidence | Model reviewed, but model/brand score not publicly visible | CHOICE Best Clothes Dryer Brand 2025; above-average reliability and satisfaction | Insufficient recent CHOICE responses/models for Best Brand assessment |
| Indicative cited price | $2,399 RRP/CHOICE price | $1,799 CHOICE price | No defensible Australian price established |
| VEU discount | Potentially about $70, subject to current register and provider | Potentially about $70, subject to current register and provider | Unlikely unless exact supplied model is on both required Australian registers |

Bosch specifications and discontinuation:  
https://media3.bosch-home.com/Documents/specsheet/en-AU/WTX88M20AU.pdf  
https://www.bosch-home.com.au/en/product/washersanddryers/tumbledryers/heatpumpdryers/WTX88M20AU

LG product information:  
https://www.lg.com/au/washer-dryers/dryers/dvh9-09w/

Samsung UK specification:  
https://www.samsung.com/uk/business/washers-and-dryers/dryers/tumble-dryer-dv90t6240ln-dv90t6240lh-s1/

---

## 2. Energy use at Victorian electricity prices

### Rate used

For a central Melbourne terrace, CitiPower is the most likely distribution zone, although the address should be checked. The 2026–27 Victorian Default Offer flat usage tariff for CitiPower is **$0.2596/kWh including GST**. Other Melbourne/Victorian zones range from $0.2735/kWh in United Energy to $0.3198/kWh in AusNet, so actual costs may be higher outside CitiPower.

Source: Essential Services Commission 2026–27 tariffs:  
https://www.esc.vic.gov.au/electricity-and-gas/prices-tariffs-and-benchmarks/victorian-default-offer

The daily supply charge is excluded because buying a dryer does not normally create an incremental electricity connection charge.

### Australian label interpretation

Bosch states that its 98 kWh/year figure is for Cottons, Cupboard Dry+, drying level 1, used once weekly and tested under AS/NZS 2442.2. Thus:

- Bosch energy per labelled cycle = 98 ÷ 52 = **1.885 kWh**
- LG energy per labelled cycle = 129 ÷ 52 = **2.481 kWh**

The LG 129 kWh/year and nine-star rating are reported by CHOICE:  
https://www.choice.com.au/products/home-and-living/laundry-and-cleaning/dryers/lg-dvh9-09w

The Bosch result is in its Australian specification:  
https://media3.bosch-home.com/Documents/specsheet/en-AU/WTX88M20AU.pdf

### Annual consumption at 6–8 loads per week

Annual cycles are:

- 6 weekly: 6 × 52 = **312 cycles**
- 7 weekly: 7 × 52 = **364 cycles**
- 8 weekly: 8 × 52 = **416 cycles**

#### Bosch

At seven weekly loads:

- 98 × 7 = **686 kWh/year**
- 686 × $0.2596 = **$178.09/year**

Range:

| Weekly loads | Annual energy | Annual CitiPower cost | Ten-year cost |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 6 | 588 kWh | $152.64 | $1,526 |
| 7 | 686 kWh | $178.09 | $1,781 |
| 8 | 784 kWh | $203.53 | $2,035 |

#### LG

At seven weekly loads:

- 129 × 7 = **903 kWh/year**
- 903 × $0.2596 = **$234.42/year**

Range:

| Weekly loads | Annual energy | Annual CitiPower cost | Ten-year cost |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 6 | 774 kWh | $200.93 | $2,009 |
| 7 | 903 kWh | $234.42 | $2,344 |
| 8 | 1,032 kWh | $267.91 | $2,679 |

#### Bosch versus LG

On the Australian label basis, Bosch saves:

- 129 − 98 = **31 kWh per labelled year**
- At seven times the label frequency: 31 × 7 = **217 kWh/year**
- Annual saving: 217 × $0.2596 = **$56.33**
- Ten-year saving: approximately **$563**

That energy saving is much smaller than the cited $600 purchase-price difference between the $2,399 Bosch and $1,799 LG. Energy alone therefore does not recover the Bosch premium within ten years.

### Samsung estimate and comparability warning

The UK data give **1.54 kWh per cycle**, a 220-minute cycle and 194 kWh annual consumption. Using 1.54 kWh directly:

| Weekly loads | Annual energy | Annual CitiPower cost | Ten-year cost |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 6 | 480.5 kWh | $124.73 | $1,247 |
| 7 | 560.6 kWh | $145.52 | $1,455 |
| 8 | 640.6 kWh | $166.31 | $1,663 |

However, these are **not Australian AS/NZS results**. A newer European EPREL record reports 1.05 kWh weighted consumption and 64 dB, whereas the older UK material reports 1.54 kWh and 63 dB. Different regulatory test methods, model revisions or program definitions make these figures unsuitable for a direct purchasing comparison with the Bosch and LG Australian labels:  
https://eprel.ec.europa.eu/screen/product/tumbledryers20232534/2200527

Actual household consumption for every machine will also depend on washer spin speed, load mass, mixed fabrics, room temperature, chosen dryness level and filter cleanliness. The LG manual specifically cautions that a small or warm room can extend drying time and increase energy use.

---

## 3. Drying performance: cotton, synthetics and wool

### What AS/NZS 2442.1 does—and does not establish

AS/NZS 2442.1:2021 specifies the laboratory procedure and minimum performance criteria for household rotary dryers, including energy and moisture measurements. AS/NZS 2442.2 covers energy-efficiency labelling. The current method incorporates the cooling period through program termination, uses a 230 V test supply, and requires rated capacity to be dried without user intervention.

Official overview:  
https://www.energyrating.gov.au/industry-information/products/clothes-dryers

Crucially, the public energy-label results are based on the supplier’s nominated standard drying program and standard textile load. They are **not separate certified wool, cotton and synthetic performance scores**. No source gathered provides AS/NZS 2442.1 final-moisture, drying-time and energy results for all three fabric types for these exact machines.

It would therefore be misleading to claim, for example, that one machine achieved a certified AS/NZS wool-drying score superior to another. The defensible comparison is as follows.

### Cotton

- **Bosch:** The Australian 98 kWh/year claim specifically identifies Cottons, Cupboard Dry+, dryness level 1. This is the strongest published Australian energy result of the three.
- **LG:** Its 129 kWh/year Australian label result indicates higher standard-cycle energy use, although it has a larger 9 kg rated capacity.
- **Samsung:** Its older EU/UK cotton-style standard cycle is reported at 220 minutes and 1.54 kWh, but this cannot be equated to an Australian AS/NZS result.

CHOICE has tested the Bosch and LG and lists measured energy/load, drying time, final moisture and drying scores, but the model-level figures are member-only. The public pages confirm that such tests exist but do not disclose results:  
https://www.choice.com.au/products/home-and-living/laundry-and-cleaning/dryers/bosch-wtx88m20au  
https://www.choice.com.au/products/home-and-living/laundry-and-cleaning/dryers/lg-dvh9-09w

### Synthetics and mixed fabrics

- **Bosch:** Includes Easy Care, Delicates, Mixed Load, Sportswear and a 40-minute mixed synthetic/light-fabric program. Its Low Heat option is designed for delicate and synthetic fabrics.
- **LG:** Provides sensor-controlled programs and an Eco Hybrid choice between lower energy and shorter drying time. Mixed loads may take longer because the sensor has to accommodate fabrics drying at different rates.
- **Samsung:** Lists Synthetics, Mixed Load, Delicates/Silk, Shirts and quick programs. OptimalDry uses moisture and temperature sensing.

For all three, separating heavy cottons from lightweight synthetics should improve consistency. A mixed load can cause synthetics to overdry while heavier seams and waistbands remain damp.

### Wool

- **Bosch:** Has a “Wool Finish” function. The word “finish” is important: it should not be assumed to fully dry every machine-washable wool garment. Care labels still govern.
- **LG:** Offers fabric-specific/delicate operation, but no comparative AS/NZS wool result was located.
- **Samsung:** Lists a Wool program, but again no Australian standard wool test was established.

For valuable knitwear, the safest practice remains a low-temperature wool program only where the care label permits tumble drying, followed by flat drying if necessary. None of the gathered evidence supports choosing one model on certified wool performance.

### Practical capacity effect

At 6–8 loads weekly, LG and Samsung’s 9 kg drums provide more headroom for towels and bedding than Bosch’s 8 kg drum. If a nominal 9 kg washer is regularly filled, the Bosch may require loads to be split; doing so could eliminate part of its apparent energy advantage. Conversely, labels measured at rated conditions do not reliably predict efficiency for frequent small loads.

---

## 4. Noise and shared-wall compliance

### Published source levels

- Bosch: **62 dB(A)**
- Samsung: **63 dB** in the UK specification; newer EPREL entry says 64 dB
- LG: no reliable exact-model manufacturer sound-power figure was found in the evidence

Bosch source:  
https://media3.bosch-home.com/Documents/specsheet/en-AU/WTX88M20AU.pdf

These are appliance test values, not the sound level that will be experienced in the adjoining terrace. Structure-borne vibration through a timber floor or masonry party wall can matter more than a one- or two-decibel nameplate difference.

### Victorian legal position

A clothes dryer is most reasonably treated as electrical equipment falling within item group 6 of regulation 114 where it is not otherwise classified. If it can be heard in a habitable room of another residence, prohibited hours are:

- Monday–Friday: before 7 am and after 8 pm
- Weekends/public holidays: before 9 am and after 8 pm

Regulation:  
https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/vic/consol_reg/epr2021393/s114.html

The Environment Protection Act also allows noise to be unreasonable outside the prohibited hours depending on its volume, duration, character and circumstances. During prohibited hours, audibility in another residence’s habitable room is sufficient; there is no simple “dryer must be below X dB” shared-wall exemption:  
https://posh.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/vic/consol_act/epa2017284/s167.html

### Installation measures for a terrace

1. Do not place the dryer directly against the party wall.
2. Level all four feet precisely; rocking creates low-frequency transmission.
3. Use a dense, purpose-made anti-vibration mat rather than soft foam that makes the dryer unstable.
4. Avoid a lightweight timber cupboard that can act as a resonant enclosure.
5. Keep hoses and the power lead from tapping the wall.
6. Schedule cycles to finish before 8 pm.
7. Perform a neighbour-side audibility check with a normal mixed load, not an empty drum.

Bosch has the best documented acoustic case. LG cannot be declared compliant without an exact sound figure and installation assessment. Samsung’s 63–64 dB is close to Bosch on paper, but its compliance and support uncertainties outweigh the small nominal difference.

---

## 5. Reliability, warranties and consumer claims

### CHOICE evidence

CHOICE’s 2020 survey covered 6,009 members, with 3,270 reporting on a dryer bought new. By technology:

- Heat-pump dryer reliability: **79%**
- Heat-pump dryer satisfaction: **89%**

These are owner assessments adjusted for product age, not laboratory failure-rate measurements. They also cover the dryer type rather than these exact models:  
https://www.choice.com.au/home-and-living/laundry-and-cleaning/dryers/articles/clothes-dryer-reliability

More recent CHOICE evidence names **LG as Best Clothes Dryer Brand for 2025**, with an average test score of 87% and above-average reliability and satisfaction. CHOICE says Samsung did not have enough tested models or survey responses for Best Brand status:  
https://www.choice.com.au/shopping/everyday-shopping/bargain-hunting/articles/best-brands-in-australia

No publicly visible exact reliability percentage was available for the Bosch WTX88M20AU or LG DVH9-09W; those fields are behind CHOICE’s member access. It is consequently not justified to invent model-specific failure rates.

### Bosch

Bosch provides a two-year Australian warranty in addition to Australian Consumer Law rights:  
https://www.bosch-home.com.au/en/c/legal/blt2b8f5ba58b132fcf/metapages/warranty

Consumer reviews of Bosch Serie 8 heat-pump dryers repeatedly allege:

- condensate-container/full-tank errors when the tank is not full;
- lint or residue accumulating in inaccessible parts of the self-cleaning system;
- declining drying performance;
- pump, sensor or control-board repairs;
- quoted repairs around $500, and one related model report of about $800 for a board and sensor.

These are self-selected anecdotes, not a representative warranty-claim rate. Some reviewers also report Bosch paying for repairs or replacement outside the written warranty, which is a positive service signal. The evidence nevertheless identifies the inaccessible condenser/condensate circuit as a plausible long-term risk:  
https://www.productreview.com.au/listings/bosch-serie-8-heat-pump-tumble-dryers

### LG

LG offers:

- two years parts and labour on the product;
- a further eight years parts-only on the inverter compressor and motor.

The extra coverage does not cover diagnosis, labour, transport or unrelated components such as pumps, sensors, bearings and control electronics:  
https://www.lg.com/au/washer-dryers/dryers/dvh9-09w/

LG has the strongest broad reliability evidence because of its 2025 CHOICE Best Brand result. No public exact-model warranty-claim frequency was found.

### Samsung

Samsung Australia generally lists washing machines and clothes dryers with a **24-month warranty**. Its longer inverter warranty depends on product and purchase date:  
https://www.samsung.com/au/support/warranty/

That warranty should not be assumed for a UK/EU DV90T6240LH/S1 or another grey-import suffix. The buyer should obtain written confirmation from Samsung Australia using the complete model code and serial number before purchase.

### Australian Consumer Law

A two-year written warranty is not a hard end to consumer rights. Goods must be of acceptable quality and durable for a reasonable period considering price, representations and expected use. An expensive dryer suffering a major failure shortly after two years may still attract a repair, replacement or refund remedy under the Australian Consumer Law.

Consumer Affairs Victoria’s whitegoods guide:  
https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/library/publications/businesses/fair-trading/electrical-and-whitegoods-an-industry-guide-to-the-australian-consumer-law.pdf

Keep the invoice, delivery record, serial number, maintenance history, photographs/video of errors, and all service correspondence.

---

## 6. Condenser cleaning and routine maintenance

### Bosch

Bosch says the condenser automatically cleans itself and does not require normal manual condenser cleaning. However, the owner must still:

- clean the fluff filter after the drying program or when prompted;
- clean the condensation-container filter;
- keep the base unit and air openings clear;
- clean the moisture sensor as directed;
- run basic or intensive appliance-care programs when required.

Manual:  
https://media3.bosch-home.com/Documents/9001786564_A.pdf

The advantage is low routine condenser labour. The disadvantage is that deeper lint accumulation may require partial dismantling by a technician because the exchanger is not designed as a simple owner-cleanable component.

### LG

LG’s automatic condenser-clean function operates during drying. LG explicitly warns that condenser cleanliness may vary with operating conditions. The dual lint filter should be cleaned **after every use**, and the model includes a condenser-care function:  
https://www.lg.com/au/washer-dryers/dryers/dvh9-09w/

This is the best maintenance compromise in the comparison: everyday filter cleaning remains essential, but routine manual brushing of exposed heat-exchanger fins is not normally required.

### Samsung

Samsung requires more owner maintenance:

- clean the lint filter after every load;
- clean the heat exchanger when prompted;
- Samsung’s general guidance recommends at least monthly cleaning, approximately every 25 cycles, or more frequently where indicated.

At 6–8 loads weekly, 25 cycles occurs roughly every 3–4 weeks. The heat exchanger must be brushed or carefully vacuumed without bending its fins:  
https://www.samsung.com/au/support/home-appliances/cleaning-the-heat-exchanger-on-a-samsung-dryer/

The manual access is a maintenance burden, but also permits an owner to remove visible lint rather than depending entirely on an automatic flushing system.

---

## 7. Australian parts and service availability

### Bosch

Bosch has an Australian customer-care operation and states that factory service and service partners continue after warranty. Nevertheless, the WTX88M20AU is officially “no longer available.” Common filters and pumps may remain obtainable, but model-specific electronics and assemblies could become slower or more expensive over a ten-year horizon.

Before buying clearance stock, request written availability and prices for:

- lint and condensation filters;
- drain pump;
- belt and tensioner;
- moisture sensors;
- electronic control module;
- complete heat-pump or compressor assembly.

### LG

The DVH9-09W has an active Australian product and support page, downloadable manuals and service booking. This gives it the lowest current parts-availability risk of the three. The ten-year compressor/motor parts warranty also gives LG an incentive to retain those particular assemblies, although it does not guarantee availability of every control board or sensor.

### Samsung

At least one Australian parts supplier lists a genuine door component specifically for DV90T6240LH/S3, available by special order with an indicated 3–10 business-day dispatch estimate:  
https://www.sydneyappliance.com.au/shop/parts/cover-doordv90t6240lh-s3abst2-5ebony/

That demonstrates some parts-channel presence, but not comprehensive Australian support. The absence of a clearly established current Samsung Australia page for the exact model is a material risk for compressors, boards and model-specific heat-pump components.

---

## 8. Installation in a heritage-listed terrace

### Ventilation and moisture

All three are condenser/heat-pump machines and normally require **no exhaust duct through an external wall**. That is particularly valuable where:

- the terrace has limited cross-ventilation;
- an external grille would be visible from the street;
- drilling Victorian-era brickwork would affect significant fabric;
- the laundry adjoins another residence.

“Ventless” does not mean “no ventilation required.” The room must still dissipate appliance heat and residual humidity. Samsung’s cited condensation efficiency is about 87%, meaning not every gram of extracted water necessarily reaches the tank or drain under the European test. The LG manual states that high room temperature and a small room can increase cycle time and energy use.

Practical requirements are:

- leave the manufacturer’s side, rear and front air clearances;
- do not install in a sealed cupboard without transfer grilles;
- provide a door undercut, louvred door or discreet internal transfer grille;
- keep the ambient temperature within the manufacturer’s limits—LG specifies 5–35°C;
- connect the drain hose to a lawful internal waste where possible, avoiding repeated tank emptying;
- use a properly earthed 230 V socket, not an extension lead;
- confirm floor capacity and level, particularly on an old suspended timber floor.

Bosch has a 600 W connection rating and 10 A protection requirement. A dedicated outlet is preferable, especially if the washer shares the laundry.

### Space

- Bosch is the shallowest confirmed Australian unit at 613 mm cabinet depth and is advantageous in a narrow terrace.
- LG is substantially deeper at 690 mm and requires 1,115 mm with its door open. Door swing and passage clearance need measurement before purchase.
- Samsung is listed at 600 mm deep, but installation clearances and hose projections will increase that figure.

None should be wall-mounted. Stacking requires the manufacturer-approved kit, a compatible washer and confirmation that the floor and old wall/floor structure can tolerate the combined load and vibration.

### Heritage overlay

City of Melbourne guidance says a Heritage Overlay does not prohibit change, but a planning permit may be needed to construct works or externally alter a building. Owners should check Clause 43.01 and the property-specific schedule and seek council planning advice:  
https://www.melbourne.vic.gov.au/heritage-owners-guide-building-and-development

Internal work usually does not require a heritage permit unless the property has uncommon internal heritage controls. An external dryer vent, new visible grille, drain penetration, external pipe or other façade alteration may constitute works or an external alteration. Equipment or services should normally be:

- internal where possible;
- placed at the rear or in a concealed lightwell;
- not visible from the principal street;
- attached through existing openings rather than significant masonry;
- reversible and colour-matched if visible.

Victorian planning guidance specifically recognises construction and installation of domestic services within Heritage Overlays as a planning category:  
https://www.planning.vic.gov.au/guides-and-resources/guides/all-guides/vicsmart-permits/accordion/buildings-and-works-in-a-heritage-overlay

The safest heritage solution is therefore a ventless dryer draining to an existing internal laundry waste, with no external wall penetration. Confirm requirements with the relevant council because many “Melbourne” terraces are in Yarra, Port Phillip, Stonnington or Boroondara rather than the City of Melbourne.

---

## 9. Victorian Energy Upgrades discount

The Victorian Energy Upgrades program’s indicative clothes-dryer discount is **$70**. Eligibility requires:

- a Victorian household or business;
- a dryer of at least seven stars and at least 5 kg capacity;
- the exact model to be on both the GEMS register and the Essential Services Commission product register;
- assignment of the certificates through an accredited provider;
- only one household high-efficiency dryer incentive.

The final discount varies with certificate price and provider costs. Retrospective assistance may be available for eligible dryers purchased from 16 December 2024:  
https://www.energy.vic.gov.au/victorian-energy-upgrades/products/clothes-dryer-discounts

Bosch and LG satisfy the headline capacity/star thresholds, but the current ESC listing must still be verified before purchase. Bosch’s discontinued status may complicate finding eligible new stock. The Samsung should be treated as ineligible unless the exact Australian suffix appears on both registers.

---

## 10. Ten-year total cost of ownership

### Assumptions

The following is a transparent planning model, not a prediction:

- CitiPower flat usage rate: $0.2596/kWh, held constant in nominal terms.
- 6–8 loads weekly.
- Purchase prices: Bosch $2,399 and LG $1,799 from the cited Australian/CHOICE listings.
- VEU discount: $70 where the exact model and transaction qualify.
- No financing, electricity-price escalation, discount rate or resale value.
- Owner cleans filters and drains at no charged labour cost.
- A **$500 ten-year maintenance/repair allowance** is included for each locally supported machine, equivalent to two $250 inspections/minor interventions. Actual cost may be zero or substantially higher.
- No full appliance replacement is assumed.
- Samsung purchase price is left as an unknown landed Australian cost because no defensible local price was established.

### Bosch TCO

Net acquisition:

- $2,399 − $70 = **$2,329**

Ten-year TCO:

| Usage | Purchase after VEU | Electricity | Maintenance allowance | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 6 loads/week | $2,329 | $1,526 | $500 | **$4,355** |
| 7 loads/week | $2,329 | $1,781 | $500 | **$4,610** |
| 8 loads/week | $2,329 | $2,035 | $500 | **$4,864** |

A single reported-type $800 board/sensor repair instead of the $500 allowance would add $300, producing a seven-load TCO of approximately **$4,910**.

### LG TCO

Net acquisition:

- $1,799 − $70 = **$1,729**

Ten-year TCO:

| Usage | Purchase after VEU | Electricity | Maintenance allowance | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 6 loads/week | $1,729 | $2,009 | $500 | **$4,238** |
| 7 loads/week | $1,729 | $2,344 | $500 | **$4,573** |
| 8 loads/week | $1,729 | $2,679 | $500 | **$4,908** |

At the midpoint, LG is about **$37 cheaper** than Bosch in this model. The difference is too small to be decisive because street prices, load sizes and one repair can reverse it. At six loads weekly LG is cheaper; at eight, Bosch’s energy advantage almost offsets its higher purchase price.

### Samsung TCO

Using the older European 1.54 kWh/cycle result:

- Six-load electricity: **$1,247 over ten years**
- Seven-load electricity: **$1,455**
- Eight-load electricity: **$1,663**

Because no reliable Australian purchase price or VEU eligibility was established:

| Usage | Ten-year TCO expression |
|---|---:|
| 6 loads/week | **Landed purchase price + $1,247 + maintenance/import-risk allowance** |
| 7 loads/week | **Landed purchase price + $1,455 + maintenance/import-risk allowance** |
| 8 loads/week | **Landed purchase price + $1,663 + maintenance/import-risk allowance** |

A minimum $500 maintenance allowance would produce landed price plus $1,747–$2,163, but a grey import deserves a larger contingency for freight, electrical compliance, diagnostic labour and unavailable assemblies. Its apparently low calculated electricity cost does not compensate for the absence of comparable AS/NZS data and confirmed local warranty support.

### TCO uncertainty

Over ten years the household will run approximately **3,120–4,160 cycles**. At that duty, condenser cleanliness, sensor condition and mechanical wear are significant. The calculations exclude:

- replacement after a non-economic compressor or board failure;
- professional installation or stacking kit;
- cupboard ventilation works;
- heritage/planning advice;
- electricity-price changes;
- extra Bosch cycles if 9 kg washer loads must be split;
- extra energy caused by low washer spin speed or poor filter maintenance.

A reasonable decision range is therefore several hundred dollars wider than the point estimates.

---

## 11. Final recommendation

### Recommended: LG DVH9-09W

Choose the LG if:

- a 690 mm cabinet depth and 1,115 mm open-door clearance fit;
- the seller confirms the current VEU listing;
- an acoustic check shows no objectionable shared-wall vibration.

Reasons:

1. 9 kg capacity better suits a high-use household.
2. Current Australian product, support and parts infrastructure.
3. CHOICE’s strongest available brand-reliability endorsement.
4. Automatic condenser cleaning plus owner-cleanable dual lint filters.
5. Ten-year compressor and motor parts cover.
6. Lower purchase price largely offsets higher energy consumption.
7. Ventless installation avoids a heritage façade penetration.

### Alternative: Bosch WTX88M20AU

Choose Bosch where:

- the laundry is shallow;
- verified 62 dB(A) operation is important;
- eight kilograms is sufficient;
- clearance or new old stock is attractively priced;
- the seller confirms parts availability and VEU eligibility.

It is the energy and documented-noise leader, but paying the full $2,399 price is difficult to justify against the LG. Obtain written assurance about service of the self-cleaning condenser/condensate system, given the recurring consumer reports.

### Not recommended without further proof: Samsung DV90T6240LH

Do not buy this exact Samsung solely because a marketplace or importer advertises a low price. Require all of the following first:

- Australian Regulatory Compliance Mark and 230 V/50 Hz documentation;
- exact Australian model suffix;
- GEMS and ESC/VEU register entries;
- written Samsung Australia warranty confirmation;
- confirmed local availability of the compressor, heat exchanger and control board;
- total landed price including delivery and installation.

Without those items, it is not a like-for-like Australian competitor to the Bosch and LG, and its European energy figures should not be used to claim superior AS/NZS drying performance.

final.content:
This is not a normal “adjustment” reaction. Worsening wheezing, chest tightness, or gasping within minutes of a new rescue inhaler can indicate paradoxical bronchospasm—an uncommon but potentially life-threatening narrowing of the airways caused by the inhaled medication or formulation. It can also reflect a serious asthma flare, an allergic reaction, or an inhaler/device problem.

What to do now

- If you are currently gasping, very short of breath, unable to speak normally, becoming drowsy/confused, developing blue or gray lips, or your oxygen is around 91%: call emergency services now (911/999 or your local number). Do not drive yourself. Sit upright while waiting.
- Because this particular inhaler repeatedly makes breathing worse immediately after use, do not take another “test” dose or keep using it to see whether you adjust. The official albuterol label says suspected paradoxical bronchospasm requires immediate discontinuation and alternative therapy; it may occur with a new canister (DailyMed/FDA label: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=d617e361-5c03-45ac-9bbe-0fa418edb19f).
- You still need an effective rescue treatment, so do not simply stop it and wait at home. You need urgent in-person assessment today—preferably an emergency department given the gasping and oxygen readings—where clinicians can confirm the inhaler’s identity, check oxygen and lung function, and provide an alternative bronchodilator, nebulized medicine, oxygen, or steroids if necessary.
- Do not stop any separate daily controller/preventer inhaler or steroid unless a clinician tells you to.
- Bring the new inhaler, its carton/leaflet, all other inhalers, and a medication list. Tell clinicians the exact timing of symptoms, the switch date, prior and current brands, dose counter, and whether there has been rash, facial/tongue swelling, throat tightness, dizziness, or a racing/irregular heartbeat.

About the oxygen reading

A home saturation of 91% is below the level at which MedlinePlus advises contacting a clinician—92% or lower—and you also have significant respiratory symptoms (https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/pulse-oximetry/). Home devices can be inaccurate by roughly 2–4 percentage points and readings can be affected by cold fingers, poor circulation, nail polish, movement, tobacco use, and skin pigmentation. Nevertheless, the FDA says not to dismiss worsening symptoms based on possible device error (https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/products-and-medical-procedures/pulse-oximeters). Your downward trend from about 95% to 91%, combined with gasping after treatment, is clinically concerning.

NIH guidance says to call emergency services when asthma medicine is not relieving symptoms or breathing remains very hard, and to go to the emergency department when symptoms do not resolve soon after home treatment (https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/asthma/attacks).

Bottom line: stop using the specific inhaler that immediately worsens your breathing, but do not remain without medical rescue treatment. With gasping and readings near 91%, seek emergency evaluation now rather than waiting for your body to adjust.

final.content:
# Mesa Group Consulting’s Use of SuperMoney and Novae

## Executive conclusion

Evert Calderon and Mesa Group Consulting are most likely using **SuperMoney and Novae as third-party product, fulfillment, and affiliate-monetization infrastructure**.

Mesa is not itself making the consumer loans, refinancing auto or student loans, issuing credit cards, underwriting insurance, or necessarily negotiating all debts. Instead, its model appears to be:

1. Attract consumers through Mesa-branded pages, consultations, credit-repair services, and educational content.
2. Determine what the consumer needs.
3. Route the consumer into a comparison marketplace or specialized provider.
4. Receive a commission or referral fee if the consumer selects, applies for, obtains, or enrolls in an eligible product.
5. Keep the customer relationship under the broader Mesa brand and potentially cross-sell Mesa’s own credit repair, consulting, monitoring, or business-funding services.

The evidence is unusually direct. Mesa’s own affiliate disclosure says:

- **SuperMoney** supplies comparisons for personal loans, auto refinancing, student-loan refinancing, debt-consolidation loans, and credit cards.
- **Novae** supplies business funding and personal/business debt-relief services.
- Mesa may receive commissions when referred customers select products, secure funding, or enroll in debt relief.

See Mesa’s affiliate disclosure: https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/affiliate-disclosure

The categories written on the Miro board therefore appear to be an implementation plan for a **Mesa-branded financial marketplace or “financial concierge” funnel**, rather than evidence that Mesa will manufacture all these products itself.

---

## 1. What SuperMoney is

SuperMoney is a consumer financial-product comparison marketplace and a business-to-business monetization platform for publishers, fintech companies, merchants, and other businesses with an audience.

Its consumer side lets users compare products such as:

- Personal loans
- Credit cards
- Auto-loan refinancing
- Student-loan refinancing
- Debt-consolidation loans
- Banking and other financial products

Its publisher side lets another company place tracked links, co-branded pages, comparison widgets, and loan prequalification tools on that company’s own website.

SuperMoney describes three relevant publisher products:

- **Super Links:** tracked affiliate links and co-branded offer pages.
- **Money Marketplace:** financial-product comparison widgets embedded in the publisher’s site or app.
- **Pre-qualification Platform:** financing offers shown to users, potentially without sending them away from the publisher’s branded experience.

SuperMoney explicitly says publishers “earn commissions when your users find products through you”: https://help.supermoney.com/article/33-how-can-i-partner-with-supermoney

Its affiliate page says publishers can monetize traffic through static links and real-time personal-loan prequalification while keeping the publisher’s brand “front-and-center”: https://www.supermoney.com/monetize

Its Super Links description says a publisher can use a provided tracking link, send visitors into more than 50 financial-service categories, and earn a commission: https://www.supermoney.com/monetize/super-links

### How SuperMoney itself makes money

SuperMoney says that when a user takes a financial product through its marketplace, the provider may pay SuperMoney a commission. It also acknowledges that compensation can influence which products appear and their placement, although comparing offers and checking prequalified rates are free to the user: https://help.supermoney.com/article/61-what-does-supermoney-do

That means the likely commercial chain is:

**Consumer → Mesa webpage/tracking link → SuperMoney marketplace → lender or card provider**

Compensation can then flow in the opposite direction:

**Provider → SuperMoney → Mesa affiliate/referral payment**

The exact amount and triggering event are not public in the evidence reviewed. It may differ by product and could be based on a qualified lead, completed application, approved account, funded loan, or another conversion event.

---

## 2. How Mesa is using SuperMoney

This relationship is confirmed by Mesa’s own legal and marketing materials.

Mesa’s terms describe “consumer loan comparison and referral services” offered through financial comparison platforms, covering:

- Personal loans
- Auto-loan refinancing
- Student-loan refinancing
- Debt-consolidation loans
- Credit-card comparisons

Mesa states that it is not the lender and that rates, terms, conditions, and lending decisions come from third-party lenders: https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/terms-and-conditions

Mesa’s disclaimer identifies SuperMoney by name as the financial-product comparison partner for exactly these five categories: https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/disclaimer

Mesa’s privacy policy further says it may share basic information with SuperMoney for product recommendations and comparisons, and that information needed for loan applications or prequalification may pass to lenders through SuperMoney or another lending network: https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/privacy-policy

### Miro-board interpretation

| Planned Mesa page | Likely SuperMoney function | Confidence |
|---|---|---:|
| Credit cards | Card comparison page or widget with tracked Mesa attribution | Very high |
| Personal loans | Multi-lender prequalification/comparison engine | Very high |
| Auto-loan refinancing | Comparison/referral to participating refinance providers | Very high |
| Student-loan refinancing | Comparison/referral to participating refinance providers | Very high |
| Debt-consolidation loan | Personal-loan marketplace presented specifically for consolidating debt | Very high |

These five Miro entries match Mesa’s current SuperMoney disclosure almost word for word.

### What the customer probably experiences

A typical workflow is likely:

1. The customer lands on a Mesa page from search, social media, advertising, a consultation, or a credit-repair relationship.
2. Mesa explains the relevant product and invites the customer to compare or prequalify.
3. A SuperMoney widget, co-branded page, or tracked referral link collects the necessary information.
4. SuperMoney returns potential offers from multiple providers.
5. The customer chooses a provider and completes the process with that provider.
6. Mesa may receive compensation if the required conversion occurs.

Mesa’s personal-loan page describes “one short application” followed by prequalified offers from multiple lenders and discloses that Mesa may receive a referral fee when a loan is completed: https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/personal-loans

Its debt-consolidation page similarly says that Mesa is not a lender, helps users compare offers from lending partners, and may earn a referral fee when a customer completes a loan: https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/debt-consolidation-loan

### Why this is especially useful to Mesa

SuperMoney lets Mesa offer a much broader range of financial products without:

- Becoming a bank or direct lender
- Building its own lender network and comparison technology from scratch
- Performing loan underwriting
- Funding loans
- Issuing credit cards
- Individually negotiating integrations with every provider

It also gives Mesa a downstream product for credit-repair customers. Someone whose credit has improved may subsequently need a card, consolidation loan, or refinance product. Conversely, a visitor receiving poor rates can be directed back toward Mesa’s credit-improvement services.

Mesa’s personal-loan page expressly uses this positioning: compare offers now, and if the customer’s credit is holding back the rate, Mesa can help improve it for future offers.

---

## 3. What Novae is

Novae is a fintech and direct-sales company that assembles consumer and small-business financial products supplied through Novae itself and through strategic partners.

Its offerings include, among other things:

- Consumer and business debt help
- Business-credit building
- Business funding
- Personal loans
- Credit cards
- Auto and student-loan refinancing
- Credit monitoring and dispute software
- Life-insurance shopping
- Business formation and related services

Novae’s main site describes its mission as expanding access to credit, capital, entrepreneurship, and financial solutions for consumers and small businesses: https://novaemoney.com/

Novae is not simply one lender or one debt-settlement firm. It is better understood as a **financial-services distribution and affiliate platform**.

### Novae affiliate model

Novae sells paid affiliate memberships:

- **Affiliate Basic:** $199 upfront plus $49 per month; direct personal commissions.
- **Affiliate Pro:** $349 upfront plus $99 per month; personal commissions, team overrides, and potential residual or rank-based benefits.

Novae advertises potential commissions of up to $3,000 or more per referral depending on the customer’s program, but expressly states that this is not guaranteed. Its published disclosure says the average participant earned **$1,408 in 2023**: https://novaemoney.com/become-an-affiliate/

The simple annual membership calculations are:

- Basic first-year listed cost:  
  **$199 + ($49 × 12) = $787**
- Pro first-year listed cost:  
  **$349 + ($99 × 12) = $1,537**

For context only, comparing those listed costs to the disclosed $1,408 average gross participant earnings gives:

- Basic: **$1,408 − $787 = $621** before taxes and every other business or marketing expense.
- Pro: **$1,408 − $1,537 = –$129** before taxes and other expenses.

These are not estimates of Mesa’s or Calderon’s earnings. They merely illustrate that Novae’s advertised “up to $3,000+ per referral” is not a typical-income figure. We do not know which arrangement Mesa has, whether it pays standard affiliate pricing, or whether it negotiated an enterprise/co-brand agreement.

### Direct-sales/team-building component

Novae’s Pro structure includes team override commissions and rank-based residual benefits. Its affiliate terms characterize affiliates as independent contractors operating their own businesses and say commissions are based on eligible product and service sales: https://novaemoney.com/common/terms_conditions.asp?GUID=AAAD26B6-1A35-4802-A7C4-4F13A4B6AC67&st=1

Thus Novae has two possible revenue paths for an affiliate:

1. Sell or refer financial products to retail customers.
2. On eligible plans, recruit or build a sales organization and receive qualified team-based compensation.

There is evidence that Novae is a direct-selling company, not merely a conventional affiliate network. In 2025, the BBB National Programs’ Direct Selling Self-Regulatory Council reviewed earnings claims made by Novae and members of its salesforce because some statements could imply that significant earnings were typical: https://bbbprograms.org/programs/advertising/dssrc/cases/novae

Nothing reviewed establishes that Mesa is recruiting a Novae downline. Mesa’s disclosed and visible use is principally **customer-product referral and fulfillment**. Team-building is a possible Novae feature, but it should not be attributed to Calderon without additional evidence.

---

## 4. Novae’s co-brand platform and why it resembles the Miro plan

Novae markets a turnkey “Co-Brand” financial-services website package. It says the package can put another business’s brand front-and-center while Novae and its partners provide the services.

The package advertises:

- 19 tailored sales pages
- More than 20 embedded forms, applications, and lead magnets
- Business credit building
- Business funding
- Business debt relief
- Personal credit solutions
- Personal and debt-consolidation loans
- Consumer debt relief
- Auto and student-loan refinancing
- Savings accounts and credit cards

Novae describes the co-brand site as a “welcoming host for the traffic you direct to it,” guiding visitors into financial-service applications while the co-brand owner earns commissions: https://novaemoney.com/cobrand-program/

That is remarkably similar to the Miro board: a list of new, category-specific pages attached to affiliate providers.

Mesa may not be using Novae’s entire prebuilt website. Its pages appear customized to Mesa’s brand and include partners outside Novae. Nevertheless, Novae’s model explains the strategy: create a broad Mesa-branded financial-services front end while outside platforms provide the product technology, licensed functions, provider networks, and fulfillment.

---

## 5. How Mesa is using Novae

Mesa’s current disclosures identify three especially important Novae functions:

1. **Consumer debt relief**
2. **Business debt relief**
3. **Business-credit building and related business funding**

Mesa’s partner page says Novae powers Mesa programs involving business funding, personal and business debt relief, and a structured business-credit-building program: https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/our-partners

Mesa’s affiliate disclosure says it receives a commission when a customer secures funding or enrolls in debt relief through Novae: https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/affiliate-disclosure

Mesa’s business-credit page goes further, stating that:

- The program operates in partnership with Novae.
- The Business Credit Finance Suite and associated software are powered by Novae technology.
- Mesa and Mesa Group Capital provide consulting, education, software, and guidance.
- Lending decisions and credit approvals remain with outside providers.

See: https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/business-credit-builder

### Consumer debt relief

For an individual who cannot reasonably repay unsecured debt, Mesa likely captures and qualifies the lead, then refers the person through Novae or a Novae-connected debt-resolution provider.

Mesa’s disclosure describes the eligible debt-relief area as settlement and negotiation services involving credit cards, personal loans, medical bills, and collections.

Novae itself acknowledges that it is a direct marketing channel for a separate platform partner that holds the relevant debt-resolution licensing. In other words, Novae may not be the legal entity performing every settlement negotiation. Its role can be distribution and platform access, with a specialist debt-relief company handling enrollment and negotiations.

Novae’s disclosure appears on its debt-help page: https://novaemoney.com/trsolutions/debt-help

That produces a likely chain such as:

**Consumer → Mesa → Novae referral/platform → licensed debt-resolution provider**

### Business debt relief

The same structure likely applies to businesses struggling with:

- Merchant cash advances
- Business credit cards
- Vendor debts
- Business loans
- Other unaffordable commercial obligations

Novae’s business debt-help program says it assesses affordability, constructs a payment budget, and negotiates with creditors for settlements ranging from reduced balances to payment in full over time: https://novaemoney.com/business-debt-help/

Mesa’s corresponding page markets business debt relief and MCA settlement, including a stated $15,000 minimum debt criterion, while warning about credit damage, continued collections or litigation, and possible taxation of forgiven debt: https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/business-debt-relief

The page sometimes says “our team” negotiates, but Mesa’s broader disclosures identify Novae and partner networks as the relevant debt-relief providers. Therefore, “our team” should not automatically be interpreted to mean only Mesa employees are conducting creditor negotiations.

### Business credit

Novae appears to be more deeply integrated in Mesa’s business-credit product than SuperMoney is in the consumer-loan pages.

Here Mesa provides the brand, consulting, client relationship, strategy, and guidance, while Novae supplies at least part of the software, program structure, business-credit education, and provider/funding infrastructure.

This is closer to a **co-delivered or white-label program** than a simple outbound affiliate link.

---

## 6. Correcting the Miro-board attribution for trust, wills, and life insurance

The board apparently labels these as “Novae”:

- Trust & will plan
- Life insurance

Novae does list life insurance among the services available through its larger platform, so it is possible that an early implementation plan contemplated routing those pages through Novae.

However, Mesa’s current public legal disclosures identify different direct partners:

### Trust and will planning

Mesa identifies **Trust & Will** as its estate-planning document platform for:

- Wills
- Trusts
- Healthcare directives
- Powers of attorney

Mesa says it may receive a commission when a customer creates estate-planning documents through Trust & Will: https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/affiliate-disclosure

### Life insurance

Mesa identifies:

- **Policygenius** as its life-insurance comparison platform.
- Various insurance carriers as the entities that underwrite and issue policies.

Mesa says it may receive a commission when a customer requests quotes, applies, or purchases through these channels. It also states that Mesa itself is not a licensed insurance agent or broker: https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/disclaimer

### Best interpretation

The current likely mapping is:

| Miro entry | Most likely current backend |
|---|---|
| Trust & will plan | Trust & Will directly |
| Life insurance | Policygenius and/or participating insurance carriers |
| Debt relief | Novae and its debt-resolution partner network |
| Business debt relief | Novae and specialized business debt-help providers |
| Business credit | Novae-powered program and software |

The “Novae” notation for trust/will and life insurance may therefore be:

- An early plan that later changed;
- A shorthand for products discoverable through the broader Novae ecosystem; or
- A plan to use Novae as an intermediary even though the final consumer-facing provider is Trust & Will, Policygenius, or an insurance carrier.

Mesa’s current legal disclosures are stronger evidence of the implemented arrangement than an internal planning label.

---

## 7. Mesa’s broader business strategy

The partnerships appear to form a customer-lifecycle model.

### Stage 1: Customer acquisition

Mesa acquires customers through:

- Credit repair
- Credit education
- Business funding consultations
- Search-optimized product pages
- Social media and advertising
- Local consultations in Bakersfield
- English, Spanish, and Punjabi support

### Stage 2: Assessment and segmentation

A customer can be routed according to need:

- Inaccurate credit-report information → Mesa credit repair
- Ongoing credit tracking → SmartCredit
- Need a loan or card → SuperMoney
- Unmanageable consumer debt → Novae/partner debt relief
- Unmanageable business debt → Novae/partner business debt help
- Need business credit → Mesa/Novae program
- Need life insurance → Policygenius/carriers
- Need estate documents → Trust & Will

Mesa’s consumer-services page visibly organizes the offerings in this way: https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/for-consumers

### Stage 3: Monetization

Revenue can come from several sources:

- Mesa’s own credit-repair and consulting fees
- SmartCredit or other monitoring referrals
- SuperMoney product conversions
- Novae debt-relief enrollments
- Business-funding referral compensation
- Novae business-credit programs
- Life-insurance referrals or sales through licensed providers
- Trust & Will estate-planning referrals
- Credit-building and rent-reporting affiliates

Mesa expressly says affiliate compensation is paid by the partner and that the customer’s price is the same whether or not Mesa receives compensation: https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/disclaimer

### Stage 4: Customer retention and cross-selling

The breadth of the marketplace lets Mesa remain relevant after the original problem is addressed.

Examples:

- A credit-repair customer later applies for a better credit card.
- A consumer who cannot qualify for an affordable consolidation loan is offered credit improvement or, where appropriate, debt relief.
- A business-credit client later applies for funding.
- A funded business that becomes overextended is routed to business debt help.
- A financial-planning customer is referred for insurance or estate documents.

This makes SuperMoney and Novae both revenue sources and “product shelf” extensions.

---

## 8. Important distinctions and risks

### Mesa is not the lender

Mesa repeatedly states that it:

- Does not issue loans or lines of credit.
- Does not approve or deny applications.
- Does not set rates or terms.
- Does not control lender underwriting.

That applies to both SuperMoney-generated consumer products and third-party business funding: https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/terms-and-conditions

### Comparison does not guarantee the best offer

SuperMoney is a compensated marketplace. It acknowledges that provider compensation can affect which products appear and their placement. Customers should still compare:

- APR
- Origination fees
- Total repayment cost
- Loan term
- Prepayment terms
- Whether the initial inquiry is soft or hard
- Whether a later formal application will create a hard inquiry

### Debt consolidation is not the same as debt relief

The Miro board correctly separates them:

- **Debt-consolidation loan:** a new loan repays existing debts. The customer generally repays the full principal, ideally at a lower rate or with a simpler payment.
- **Debt relief/debt settlement:** the customer cannot maintain current payments and attempts to settle eligible debts for less than the full amount.

Debt settlement can involve credit damage, fees, collection activity, lawsuits, and possible taxable forgiven debt. Mesa’s business debt-relief page discloses these risks.

### Affiliate incentives create conflicts

Mesa is paid when certain users convert. SuperMoney and Novae are also compensated distribution platforms. Even if the consumer pays no separate referral charge, compensation creates an incentive to recommend monetized products.

Mesa discloses that conflict, but consumers should ask:

- Is this the full market or only participating providers?
- What event produces compensation for Mesa?
- Is Mesa paid differently depending on the provider or product?
- Is there a non-affiliate alternative?
- Who legally provides and services the product?
- For debt relief, which licensed entity performs negotiations?
- For insurance, which licensed agent or broker is responsible?

### Novae income claims should be read cautiously

Novae’s “up to $3,000+ per referral” is a maximum-style marketing statement, not a typical result. Its own disclosed 2023 average participant income was $1,408, before considering affiliate fees and other expenses. The direct-selling regulator’s 2025 monitoring inquiry reinforces the need to distinguish potential earnings from typical earnings.

This concern applies to the Novae business opportunity, not necessarily to the quality or suitability of every underlying financial product.

### Some Mesa legal pages appear unfinished

Mesa’s fetched terms, privacy policy, and disclaimer displayed placeholders such as “[TBD — date of publication]” for effective or update dates. The documents nevertheless provide detailed partner disclosures, but those placeholders introduce uncertainty about final publication status and version control.

---

## 9. Bottom-line answer

Evert is not merely using SuperMoney to “find products.” Mesa is very likely enrolled as a **SuperMoney monetization/publisher partner** and is using SuperMoney’s marketplace, tracked links, co-branded pages, widgets, or prequalification technology to populate Mesa’s new pages for:

- Credit cards
- Personal loans
- Auto-loan refinancing
- Student-loan refinancing
- Debt-consolidation loans

Mesa earns or may earn referral compensation when users select or complete eligible products.

Novae is a broader **affiliate, co-brand, fintech-software, and fulfillment platform**. Mesa is using it principally for:

- Personal debt relief
- Business debt relief
- Business-credit building
- Business funding and related infrastructure

In these areas, Mesa supplies the customer relationship, branding, consultations, and guidance, while Novae and its provider network supply software, financial-product access, specialist services, or licensed fulfillment. Mesa receives commissions or program revenue when customers enroll or obtain eligible services.

The trust/will and life-insurance notes require qualification. Mesa’s current disclosures identify **Trust & Will** as the estate-planning platform and **Policygenius/insurance carriers** for life insurance—not Novae as the final provider. The Miro labels may reflect an earlier plan or use “Novae” as a broad sourcing shorthand.

Overall, Mesa is building a **Mesa-branded financial-services distribution hub**: its own credit-repair and consulting operations sit at the center, while SuperMoney, Novae, SmartCredit, Trust & Will, Policygenius, and other providers extend the product catalog and generate referral revenue.
